column2: Tamar's beauty and relation to Absalom, and Amnon's stated love, remain the narrative introduction without an added judgment about the nature of that love.
Propose For she was a virgin to retain the explanatory hoti in Amnon's distress and perceived difficulty of doing anything to her.
Jonadab's companionship, parentage through David's brother and exceptional shrewdness remain; shrewd is the contextual rendering of wise here, not moral approval.
Morning after morning, king's son, demand for an explanation and Amnon's statement about his brother Absalom's sister retain the repeated family relationships.
Jonadab's instruction to lie down and act ill, anticipated paternal visit and request for Tamar's visible food preparation and hand-feeding remain his plan.
The narrator says Amnon became ill after lying down, then records the two little loaves requested before his eyes.
column3: The wording is not silently changed to feigned illness to harmonize it with the preceding plan; the precise narrative stance remains open.

column2: David sends Tamar to her brother's house to prepare food; the command does not state his knowledge of the scheme.
Tamar finds Amnon lying down, takes dough, mixes, forms and cooks the little loaves in his sight; the preparation sequence remains.
The pan is emptied before him, but he refuses to eat and commands removal of every man; the command is fulfilled before the private demand.
The inner-room request and hand-feeding pretext lead Tamar to bring the prepared loaves to her brother's bedroom, continuing into verse 11.
Tamar brings food near, Amnon seizes her and demands intercourse while calling her sister; the agent switch and coercive seizure remain.
Propose For such a thing must not be done in Israel to retain the explanatory dioti. Her initial No, brother address, prohibition of violation and folly remain.
column3: Must not interprets the negative future normatively in her protest, not as a narrator's claim that such violence never happens.

column2: Tamar's disgrace question, warning of folly and plea to speak to the king retain her emphatic assertion that he will not withhold her.
column3: The assertion is her appeal in the scene; the translation does not turn it into an independent legal finding about marriage permissions.

column2: Amnon refuses her voice, overpowers her, violates her and lies with her; the explicit coercion and agency remain without euphemism or attributed consent.
Propose For the hatred to preserve the causal explanation that the hatred exceeded the prior love. Both repeated cognate expressions and dismissal remain.
Propose For this last evil after No, brother, preserving her explanation that sending her away is greater than the first evil. His renewed refusal to listen remains.
The household supervisor receives the order to send this one outside and lock the door behind her; the demeaning demonstrative remains.
column3: The sending imperative is plural and locking singular, possibly involving household staff under the addressed servant; no extra named personnel are supplied.

column2: The wrist-reaching tunic and royal virgin daughters' outer-garment custom remain before the attendant's expulsion and locked door.
column3: The garment identification follows the selected wrist-related adjective, not a substituted many-coloured robe; detailed tailoring remains provisional.

column2: Ashes, head, torn tunic, both hands on her head and continual crying as she goes remain her visible grief.
Absalom asks about Amnon, commands silence because he is her brother and forbids setting her heart on speaking; Tamar remains living as a widow in his house.
column3: These are Absalom's words, not an endorsed response to violence. Widow language describes the selected state without inventing a prior marriage or dead husband.

column2: David's great anger and his failure to grieve Amnon's spirit remain, with love and firstborn status as the two stated reasons.
column3: The expanded selected clause is not omitted or replaced by an inferred punishment that the text does not describe.

column2: Neither evil nor good retains Absalom's refusal of speech, while hatred is explicitly linked to Tamar's violation.
Two full years, sheep shearers at Baal-hazor adjoining Ephraim and all royal sons invited remain.
Propose Behold at Absalom's introduction of the shearing, preserving the presentative and the invitation to the king and his servants.
The king refuses the whole group's attendance to avoid burdening Absalom, withstands pressure and blesses him.
Absalom's alternative invitation specifies brother Amnon, and the king asks why he should accompany him.
Pressure leads the king to send Amnon and all royal sons; the full additional royal-style drinking feast remains.
Propose For am I not the one commanding you? to retain the causal appeal supporting Do not be afraid. Wine, signal, strike-and-kill order and courage exhortation remain.
Absalom's servants obey his order against Amnon; all royal sons rise, mount individual mules and flee.
The initial report falsely claims all royal sons were struck with not even one left; it remains clearly a report, not a narrator's replacement for what happened.
David tears his clothes and lies on the ground, while every surrounding servant tears his own garments.
Propose For Amnon alone and For he had been marked out to preserve both explanatory hoti links in Jonadab's correction.
column3: Marked out by Absalom interprets the difficult lying-on-Absalom's-mouth expression; whether decree, resolve or another idiom is intended remains unresolved.

column2: Propose For only Amnon has died to preserve the explanation for rejecting the all-sons report. Only is expressly supported by the exceptive and emphatic alone wording.
Propose saw, and behold, a large crowd to retain the presentative in the watchman's view. The full added descent and Horonen-road report remain.
Behold introduces the sons' arrival and Jonadab's assertion that his servant's word has been fulfilled; ordinary human your remains.
Propose behold before the sons' arrival while Jonadab finishes; their raised voices and the king and all servants' very great weeping remain.
Absalom goes to Talmai son of Ammihud of Geshur in Machad; David's mourning for his son remains without a newly supplied son's name.
Repeated escape and Geshur destination remain with the three-year stay, not merged into the previous verse.
The king's spirit ceases going out after Absalom because he is comforted concerning dead Amnon; no longing to visit is substituted.
column3: The spirit/going-out construction and implication for pursuit remain interpretive questions, not an established reconciliation between the men.
